what: Distance feedback changes a moving robot’s commands near an obstacle. Stopping distance: compare the distance reading with the braking motion.
try: Use the example’s supplied mat and program, then Reset and run.
Compare the distance reading with the actual gap at the front of the robot.
Change the stopping threshold or speed and repeat from the same start.
why: A range measurement comes from the sensor position and direction. The chassis still moves while commands and braking take effect. A safe threshold must allow for sensor mounting and motion.
matters: Mobile robots need space to react before reaching a wall.
question: Does a sensor reading of 5 cm mean every front part is 5 cm from the wall?
answer: No. The sensor can sit behind the foremost part, and its ray measures along its own direction.
further: Compare two speeds using one threshold.
For the maze, inspect why a turn changes the next ray direction.
